title: Gabber's criterion: on a ring with strictly henselian local rings, H^1 Mayer-Vietoris injectivity on principal opens gives vanishing of all higher cohomology (Stacks 0GY0)
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $\mathcal F$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For $h\in R$ let $D(h)\subseteq S$ be the principal open subscheme, $j_h:D(h)\to S$ its open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $\mathcal F|_{D(h)}=j_h^{-1}\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; for $D(h')\subseteq D(h)$ the restriction map $H^1(D(h)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(h)})\to H^1(D(h')_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(h')})$ is the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] along the inclusion, composed with the canonical identification of the inverse images. Assume that for all $f,g\in R$ the kernel of the map
$$H^1(D(f+g)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f+g)})\longrightarrow H^1(D(f(f+g))_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f(f+g))})\oplus H^1(D(g(f+g))_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(g(f+g))})$$
(both components restriction maps) is zero. Then the etale cohomology groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] satisfy $H^q(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=0$ for all $q>0$.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 (label lemma-gabber-criterion), line 14228, and its proof (uses Lemma 09AX, label lemma-local-rings-strictly-henselian, line 14205: etale cohomology equals Zariski cohomology on a scheme with strictly henselian local rings; Cohomology Lemma 01E9 Mayer-Vietoris; induction on the degree). Stacks writes $H^1_{\Et}(D(f),\mathcal F)$ for the cohomology of the object $D(f)$ of $S_{\Et}$, which is $H^1(D(f)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f)})$ by Cohomology on Sites Lemma 03F3

proof.text: *Etale/Zariski comparison on principal opens.* By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)\to S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an open immersion with image $D(h)$, so we identify $D(h)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)$. A prime of $R_h$ is a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $h\notin\mathfrak p$; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] identifies the local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)$ at this prime with $(R_h)_{\mathfrak pR_h}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$. Hence every local ring of $D(h)$ is one of the strictly henselian local rings assumed for $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-strict-henselian-zariski-comparison] (Stacks 09AX) to $D(h)$ and to $S$. Thus etale cohomology on $S$ and on every $D(h)$ is canonically identified with the corresponding Zariski cohomology, with the comparison maps induced by the etale-to-Zariski site morphism.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 (label lemma-gabber-criterion), line 14228, proof: first sentence, applying Lemma 09AX on each open of Spec(R)

proof.text: *Induction statement with the original ring fixed.* For an integer $i\ge0$, let $P(i)$ assert that for every $h\in R$ and every $q$ with $1\le q\le i$, $H^q(D(h)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(h)})=0$. We prove $P(i)$ by induction. $P(0)$ is vacuous. Assume $P(i-1)$ and fix $h\in R$ and $\xi\in H^i(D(h)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(h)})$ for $i\ge1$. We work directly on $D(h)$, so no localization transport is assumed. For later use, an element $a/h^n\in R_h$ has principal open $D_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)}(a/h^n)=D_S(ah)\subseteq D(h)$ by the identification in step 1; thus the induction is already quantified over all principal opens of every $R_h$ without changing the original ring or its hypotheses.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 proof, induction paragraph (line 14228): prove vanishing simultaneously on all D(h); the localization identification is made explicit here so the degree-one hypothesis remains the stated hypothesis over R

proof.text: *The vanishing ideal on a fixed principal open.* Define $I_h=\{f\in R\mid \xi|_{D(hf)}=0\}$. By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-cohomology-locally-zero], $\xi$ is locally zero on the Zariski space $D(h)$. Principal opens form a basis, so for every prime $\mathfrak p$ with $h\notin\mathfrak p$ there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ with $f\in I_h$ (shrink a neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ to $D(hf)$). If $f\in I_h$ and $r\in R$, then $rf\in I_h$ because $D(hrf)\subseteq D(hf)$. We prove closure under addition next.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 proof, paragraph defining I (line 14228): Zariski local triviality and the observation that I is closed under multiplication

proof.text: *Addition in degree one.* If $i=1$ and $f,g\in I_h$, apply the assumed kernel condition to the two elements $hf$ and $hg$. Their sum is $h(f+g)$, and the two target opens are $D(h^2f(f+g))=D(hf(f+g))$ and $D(h^2g(f+g))=D(hg(f+g))$. The class $\xi|_{D(h(f+g))}$ restricts to zero on both because these opens lie in $D(hf)$ and $D(hg)$, respectively. The assumed injectivity therefore gives $\xi|_{D(h(f+g))}=0$, so $f+g\in I_h$.

source.place: Lemma 0GY0 proof, paragraph after definition of I (line 14228): for q=i=1 this is exactly the hypothesis

proof.text: *Addition in higher degree and conclusion.* Suppose $i>1$ and $f,g\in I_h$. The identity $D(h(f+g))=D(hf(f+g))\cup D(hg(f+g))$ has intersection $D(hfg(f+g))$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris] to this cover. The class $\xi|_{D(h(f+g))}$ restricts to zero on both degree-$i$ terms because the first open lies in $D(hf)$ and the second in $D(hg)$. Exactness reduces it to the preceding group $H^{i-1}(D(hfg(f+g))_{\Et},\mathcal F|)$, which is zero by $P(i-1)$; hence $f+g\in I_h$. Thus $I_h$ is an ideal. Every prime containing $I_h$ contains $h$, because every prime avoiding $h$ avoids some element of $I_h$. The prime-ideal characterization of radicals gives $h\in\sqrt{I_h}$, so $h^N\in I_h$ for some $N$ (with the case $h=0$ immediate). Then $D(h)=D(h^{N+1})$, and the definition of $I_h$ gives $\xi=0$. This proves $P(i)$, and induction gives $H^q(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks Lemma 0GY0 (etale-cohomology.tex line 14228) into five steps: identify each D(h) with Spec(R_h), identify its local rings with R_p, and apply the 09AX comparison; induct simultaneously over all principal opens D(h), avoiding an unproved localization transport; define I_h as the elements f for which the class vanishes on D(hf), use local Zariski triviality, and show every prime avoiding h avoids I_h; prove closure under addition in degree one by applying the stated kernel hypothesis to hf and hg; and prove higher-degree addition by Mayer-Vietoris, then use h in the radical of I_h to conclude the class vanishes. The proof and source places are recorded directly from the cited Stacks route.
